newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ manufacturers' confidence falls in June Qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ manufacturers' confidence falls in June Qtr.

text.p: Manufacturers' confidence deteriorated further in the June quarter, the Manufacturers Federation said on Monday.
The WestpacTrust quarterly survey for the federation showed most affected were manufacturers in the upper North Island and South island.
A net 47 percent of manufacturers reported declining profits in the latest quarter, continuing the downward trend.
The federation said profit expectations were always significantly higher than profit outcomes but a net four percent of firms tipped declining profits in the September quarter.
It added the sharp decline in profits in the first six months of 1997 was a major factor in a reduction in investment intentions.
"A net 30 percent of firms expect to spend less on plant and machinery over the next 12 months."
The federation added falling investment would restrict future growth potential.
* A net 30 percent of firms indicated they'd be cutting prices in the quarter

* Firms were continuing to cut both raw material and finished goods stocks but stock cutting forecasts for the September quarter were less than for the June three months reflecting some optimism for improved output in the September quarter
* Exporters saw little benefit from the depreciation in the trade weighted index during the March quarter.
